children.translated_text: Success, arising from the name of <s>Śrī</s>, belongs to those for whom every desired prosperity comes to be.
Having bowed to those worthy ones, I compose a commentary on the chapter of <s>Kaṅkāla</s>.
Having heard a little from teachers and having combined something from those who know the subject,
and having experienced even a little myself, this treatise is explained by me.
Even when metallic doctrine has been taught directly by the teacher, it does not succeed
until the procedure of the operation has been seen two or three times at the teacher's side.

children.text: yasmāttasmādapi śrutvā yatra kutrāpi vīkṣya ca
children.translated_text: Because, having heard it from anyone whatever and having seen it anywhere at all,
fools, spending their materials, wear themselves out in vain.
But if a true guru, becoming gracious, shows the whole operation,
then all the applications succeed, even with ease, without doubt.
Therefore here, even when the meaning of the text has been stated clearly, because certainty about the main point is essential,
one should not undertake exertion in metallic doctrine while disregarding the gurus.

children.text: vakti yo na sa jānāti yo jānāti na vakti saḥ
children.translated_text: He who speaks does not know; he who knows does not speak.

children.text: tato yatrāpi tatrāpi prasāryaṃ na mukhaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise should not open their mouth everywhere and anywhere.
One skilled in rasa-pills and collyria, worthy of the revered <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>,
communicated the truth of rasa for the instruction of his own pupil.
And a capable pupil of the revered <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>, for the benefit of himself and others,
composed the <s>Rasādhyāya</s> in twenty-one sections.
Having first bowed to revered <s>Bhairava</s>, the omniscient lord of the three worlds,
and to revered <s>Bhāratī</s> and <s>Vighneśa</s>, I praise them for the pacification of obstacles.
Celibacy and austerity must be practiced, and food fit for oblation should be eaten.

children.text: kriyābhraṣṭe na sidhyanti taponaṣṭe phalanti na ||
children.translated_text: When the procedure is spoiled, they do not succeed; when austerity is lost, they bear no fruit.
Now I state the chapter that has come down from the yogin revered <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>,
in which chain-rasa is made manifest by reasoned procedures.

children.text: sūtadoṣāṃs tataḥ śuddhiṃ saṃskārāt prāk vadāmyaham
children.translated_text: Next I shall speak of the defects of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and its purification before the saṃskāras,
the production of the effects of rasas, and the rasāyana for the body and metals.
One covering is earthen; a second covering is stony;

children.text: tṛtīyo jalajātaśca dvau dvau ca nāgavaṅgajau ||
children.translated_text: the third is water-born, and there are two each arising from lead and tin.
In tin there are the kapālī and kālikā; in lead there are the śyāmā and kapālikā.

children.text: yādṛśā ca tarā dugdhe tadrūpe dve kapālike ||
children.translated_text: And as there is a film on milk, so there are two kapālikās of that form.
Śyāmā may be five-colored; kālikā is black in color.

children.text: sadā sūtasya jāyante sahajāḥ sapta kañcukāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These seven innate coverings always arise on <s>sūta</s>.
The impurity-defect is one; the second is fire-born;
the third is the poison-defect, and the fourth is called arrogance.

children.text: unmattaḥ pañcamo doṣo doṣāḥ pañca sadā rase
children.translated_text: The fifth defect is madness; these five defects are always in rasa.

children.text: mṛṇmayāt kañcukāt kuṣṭhaṃ jāyate ca śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: From the earthen covering, skin disease arises in embodied beings.
From the stony one comes stiffness, and from the water-born one a mass of wind-disorders.
The kapālikās of tin and lead produce chilharī in the body.
The kālikā always causes elephant-skin disease and ringworms,

children.text: pāṇḍurogaṃ tathā mohaṃ dubhitāni ca kāmalām ||
children.translated_text: as well as pallor, delusion, bad disorders, and jaundice.
White leprosy arises from the śyāmā covering.
The impurity produced from mercury destroys the body's vitality.
Fire causes destruction of strength, and poison causes dizziness.
From arrogance the limbs indeed split, and from madness there comes insanity.

children.text: yuktaṃ dvādaśabhir doṣair yastu dadyāttu pāradam
children.translated_text: But he who administers mercury combined with the twelve defects
always incurs killings such as the killing of a Brahmin.
He who administers lordly mercury freed from the twelve defects

children.text: mahīyān iha loke syātparatra svargabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: becomes great in this world and in the next becomes a sharer in heaven.
Rasa, freed from the twelve defects, makes the body free of disease,
and, refined by saṃskāras equal to the number of the islands, effects the body and metals.
There are eighteen saṃskāras for <s>sūta</s>; among them the first is pāṭasāraṇa,

children.text: dvitīyo mardano nāma tṛtīyaḥ śodhano mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the second is named mardana, and the third is considered śodhana.
Mūrchana and utthāpana are the fourth; the fifth is rasapātana.
The sixth is the raising of rasa; the seventh is svedana.
The eighth is said to be niyāmaka, and the ninth is nirodhaka.

children.text: daśamo mukhakārī syāt rudrasaṃkhyo hi jāraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tenth is mukhakārī, and jāraṇa has Rudra's number, eleven.

children.text: sūryāṅko bandhakṛt prokto yakṣasaṃsthas tu sāraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Bandhakṛt is said to have the number of the suns, twelve, while sāraṇa is established in the number of the yakṣas, thirteen.
Māraṇa has Manu's number, fourteen, and pratisāraṇa has the number of the lunar dates, fifteen.
Krāmaṇa has the sixteenth number, and vedha is the seventeenth.
The eighteenth saṃskāra is considered by the experts to be udghāṭana.
When <s>sūta</s> has been filtered through cloth, the saṃskāra is pāṭasāraṇa.
All alterations such as those of tin and lead remain in the cloth.
To make <s>sūta</s> abandon blackness, loṣṭajīkaka is to be applied.
One pala of that and sixty-four palas of <s>sūta</s>
should be placed in a mortar, mixed together, and rubbed for the duration of one watch.
When rubbed, it becomes stainless and certainly gives up its blackness.
When ground with the milk of vajrī, the earth-born covering departs in seven days.
When ground for seven days with arka-milk, the stone-covering departs.
One should use the parpaṭas of the brahma-tree, moistened with water,
and when it is ground for seven days with their juice, the water-covering departs.
When ground with a decoction of citraka, the tin-born kāpālī departs.
When ground with the juice of vajrakanda itself, the tin-born kālikā departs.
When ground with the milk of bitter gourd, the lead-born śyāmā is destroyed.
When ground with bīyā-water, the kapālī born from lead is destroyed.
By being ground for seven days each, the coverings disappear from <s>sūta</s>.
When it has been ground with a decoction of triphalā, the impurity is thus brought to destruction.
When it has been ground with a decoction of citraka, the defect of fire is destroyed.
In just this way, with the juice of aśvagandhā, the defect of poison is pacified.
When it has been ground with the juice of nāhyā, the defect of pride is destroyed.
When it is ground in this way with the juice of kudhya, even madness dissolves away.

children.text: saptasaptadinaiḥ piṣṭād doṣā naśyanti pañca vai
children.translated_text: By grinding for seven days in each case, the five defects indeed disappear.

children.text: itthaṃ dvādaśabhir doṣairmuktaḥ śuddho bhaved rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>rasa</s> (mercury), freed from the twelve defects, becomes purified.
At the end of each medicine, one should wash it with sour gruel.
The purification of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is to be carried out with eleven medicines.

children.text: kvāthena trikaṭoḥ kṣuṇṇaṃ prākṛtaṃ śodhitaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: The ordinary purified mercury, pounded with a decoction of trikaṭu,
and with the juice of fresh sannadūdhilī, and also with its moist juice,
and in this way with the juice of kākamācī and with the juice of devadālī,

children.text: śuṣkaṃ śuṣkaṃ punaḥ kṣuṇṇaṃ saṃmardyāmardya śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: when dry and again dry, should be pounded again; after thoroughly rubbing and rubbing it, one should dry it.
At the end of each medicine, one should wash it with sour gruel.
Here it should be rubbed for seven days, exactly seven, with each medicine.
For <s>sūta</s>, the reviving after stupefaction is to be done with five medicines.
Mercury that has been revived from stupefaction certainly becomes powerful.
When <s>sūta</s> has the appearance of lampblack, having abandoned its dense mobility,

children.text: saṃmūrchitas tadā jñeyo nānāvarṇo 'pi tat kvacit ||
children.translated_text: then it should be known as stupefied, even if in some case it has various colors.
After confining it, one should revive it when it is placed in the middle of a sealed pair of vessels.

children.text: punas tan mūrchayet sūtaṃ kañcukīr nāśayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should stupefy that <s>sūta</s> again, and thereafter destroy the coverings.
In this order one should stupefy it seven times.
Thus stupefied, <s>sūta</s> becomes free from defects.
A knower of <s>rasa</s> should revive mercury by means of āranāla.
Of mercury that has been revived from stupefaction, there should be sixty-four palas,
and sixteen palas of copper powder should be placed in a mortar.

children.text: nimbukaṃ ca rasaṃ kṣiptvā lūnaṃ dvātriṃśadaṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: After adding lemon juice and salt amounting to a thirty-second part,

children.text: tāvat saṃmardayed yāvat pīṭhī syān mṛkṣaṇopamā
children.translated_text: one should rub it until the paste becomes like a smooth unguent.
Having placed that paste in the bottom of a cauldron, one should apply a cloth wrapping.
One should smear the ends of the cloth with clay, as though they had been digested in the bottom vessel.
One should place the cauldron inverted upon the mouth of a water-filled pot.

children.text: kaṇṭhaṃ kaṭāhabandhaṃ ca limped vastraṃ mṛdā tathā ||
children.translated_text: One should smear the neck and the binding of the cauldron, and likewise the cloth, with clay.
One should kindle cow-dung cakes from the cauldron for half a yāma.

children.text: jalamadhye raso yāti tāmraṃ tiṣṭhati bundhake ||
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> goes into the water, while the copper remains in the bottom vessel.
This should be done seven times; the distillation of mercury will become purified.
The subtle defects dissolve away in the distillation of mercury that has been revived from stupefaction.

children.text: khalvena sahitaṃ sūtaṃ mardayec ca dinatrayam
children.translated_text: One should rub the mercury together with the mortar for three days.

children.text: pūrvavatpātayettaṃ tu adhordhvaṃ tiryagaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Then one should distill it as before, downward, upward, and sideways.
Thus, by means of the distillation apparatus, one should distill it seven times.
Mercury and mica, the two, are to be rubbed all around with sour gruel.
That, made into a ball, should be placed also in the middle of the bottom of a pot.
With equal parts of triphalā, rājikā, fire-substance, poison, and śigru,
one should smear the upper pot and make an excellent sealed capsule.
At the joint, having wrapped it with clay, this is the excellent ḍamaru apparatus.
On its upper part also a special coil should be made.
Beneath it one should kindle a fire gently, gently, for three yāmas.
Leaving the lower pot, it passes into the upper pot.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ saindhavaṃ sūtaṃ tattulyaṃ ca dināvadhi
children.translated_text: Kāsīsa, rock salt, and mercury, in equal quantity, should be treated for the duration of a day.
In the absence of kāsīsa, phullatūrikā should be given.
One should throw them little by little into a mortar and rub the three together.
Each should be one hundred niṣkas, not less and never more.
With a pot-sealing apparatus one should cook it for a day with fierce fire.

children.text: ūrdhvalagnaṃ tu taṃ śuddhaṃ pāradaṃ cāharet śubham ||
children.translated_text: One should collect that pure, excellent mercury which has adhered above.

children.text: pattrāṇi tāmrasya laghūni piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā rasena triguṇena bhāṇḍe
children.translated_text: Having made thin leaves of copper into a paste with three times as much mercury in a vessel,
the mercury from the copper and the copper from the mercury are separated for distillation.

children.text: dvayaṃ tathaiva sampiṣya pīṭhī kāryā ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Having ground the two together in just the same way, a paste should be made as before.
That paste of copper and mercury should again be placed in a pot.

children.text: sthālīṃ cādhomukhīṃ tv anyāṃ limped vastramṛdā mukhe ||
children.translated_text: Another pot, facing downward, should be smeared at the mouth with cloth and clay.
That apparatus is called ḍamaruka, and likewise is known as vidyādhara.
Then cow-dung should be placed on the bottom of the upper pot.

children.text: adhaḥ sthālyāstvadho bundhe yāmaṃ mṛdvagninā pacet
children.translated_text: Below the lower pot, at the lower bottom, one should cook it with mild fire for a yāma.
The mercury goes into the upper pot, while the copper remains right there.
This is to be done seven times; it is called the raising of mercury.
Mercury that has been distilled and raised becomes penetrating and clear.
One should knead the leaves of the śigru tree with water,
so that a very soft lump is produced; one should make a small bowl from the lump.
The mercury that has risen after leaving the copper, together with salt amounting to a thirty-second part,
should be placed completely inside the small bowl made earlier.
One should put āranāla and lemon juice into a pot.
One should fasten a piece of wood at the neck, with the previously made small bowl in a cloth.

children.text: kāṣṭhe vastraṃ ca badhnīyān na spṛśetkāñjikaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: One should fasten the cloth to the piece of wood so that it does not touch the sour gruel.
When the pot is covered in that way, one should kindle a mild fire beneath it.

children.text: pratyahaṃ tv aṣṭayāmaṃ ca kāryaṃ saptadināni vai
children.translated_text: Every day, for eight yāmas, this should be done for seven days.

children.text: pratyahaṃ śigrupattraiś ca kāryā kulhaḍikā navā ||
children.translated_text: Every day a fresh small bowl should be made from śigru leaves.

children.text: naṣṭaṃ naṣṭaṃ cāranālaṃ prakṣipen nūtanaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Again and again, as the āranāla is used up, fresh āranāla should be poured in.
The procedure for heating <s>rasa</s> should be carried out by means of the <s>dolāyantra</s>.

children.text: svedanair vahnir utpanno raso jāto bubhukṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: By the heatings, fire is produced, and the <s>rasa</s> becomes hungry.
Now the upward-moving <s>rasa</s> very greatly withstands the fire during cooking.
With equal portions of rājikā, salt, vahnimūlaka, and a single rūṣaṇa,
this heating of <s>pārada</s> is extended with husk-water over a gentle fire.
With sour gruel and medicinal leaves inside, and with a bundle suspended in the middle,
that which is to be heated is heated over a hearth-fire; this is the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Having folded cloth in four layers and made it into a packet even with khaga,

children.text: svedyaṃ sūtaṃ ca mandāgnau yathā nopakṣayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: the <s>sūta</s> to be heated should be heated over a mild fire, so that it does not suffer loss.
Vyoṣa, fresh śigru root, mayūramūlaka, and āsurī

children.text: kāñjikena ca saṃsvedyaṃ sūtaṃ buddhimatā dinam ||
children.translated_text: are to be heated with sour gruel together with <s>sūta</s> for a day by an intelligent man.
With the five urines of cows, buffaloes, sheep, and donkeys,
and with the five salts and alkalis, <s>raseśvara</s> should be heated.
With cāṅgerī, sour gruel, and the juices of nimba, jambīra, and bījapūraka,
<s>pārada</s> should also be heated for the sake of opening its mouth.
In the northern direction there should be a large lump of red rock salt.

children.text: tadgarbhe randhrakaṃ kṛtvā sūtaṃ ca sveditaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made a small cavity in its interior, one should put in the heated <s>sūta</s>.
Then, after adding chickpea alkali and lemon juice on top,
one should pour in the <s>rasa</s> and place another similar rock-salt lump over it.
Having made a pit, then placing the rock-salt capsule in the ground,
one should put eight fingers of dust over it and cow-dung fuel for seven days.
After kindling the fire, one should take it out and wash it with sour gruel.

children.text: ayaṃ niyāmako nāma saṃskāro hy aṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This procedure, called niyāmaka, is remembered as the eighth saṃskāra.
When chickpea alkali is unavailable, powder born from navasāra may be used.
When that is unavailable, sājīkṣāra; when that is unavailable, the alkali of jhījaraṭa.
When that is unavailable, hiṅgupūṣā, and likewise castor fruits;

children.text: pūṣā dattvā ca pratyekaṃ prakṣipen naimbukaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: after adding pūṣā, one by one, one should pour in lemon juice.
That <s>pārada</s>, having become extremely able to withstand fire, is a niyāmaka.

children.text: annārthaṃ rasanā lolā niḥśaṅkaṃ saṃskṛtaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Its tongue is eager for food; when well prepared it is always fearless.

children.text: kācakumpe mṛdā limpen madhye niyāmakaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: One should smear a glass flask with clay and put the niyāmaka <s>rasa</s> in the middle.

children.text: kṣiptvāsye cīvaraṃ baddhvā channaṃ koḍīyakena ca ||
children.translated_text: After binding cloth over its mouth, it should be covered with a small cup.

children.text: bhūgarte kumpikāṃ kṣiptvā dattvā copari vālukām
children.translated_text: Having placed the little flask in an underground pit and put sand over it,
one should kindle a cow-dung fire every day for seven days.
The <s>rasa</s> from the little flask is to be collected; it is called nirodhaka, according to rule.
It licks with its tongue, afflicted by excessive hunger.

children.text: snuhī ca girikarṇī ca kṣīriṇī vajrakañcukī
children.translated_text: Snuhī, girikarṇī, kṣīriṇī, vajrakañcukī,
sarpākṣī, meghanādā, matsyākṣī, and mṛgabhojanī,
śiraḥpuṅkhā, cāṅgerī, vajravastrī, punarnavā,
madhuka, the two sārivās, tiktā, trāyantī, candana, and amṛtā,
forest tulasī, kṛṣṇā, śākhinī, and ravibhūlikā:
these are called yamikā herbs in <s>rasa</s>-work by <s>Śambhu</s>.
From among these restraining herbs, one should prepare what is available.
It will certainly become wing-clipped through the auspicious cooking with the herb.
Next I shall state the niyāmikā herbs for the killing operation of <s>sūta</s>.
Sarpākṣī, kṣīriṇī, vandhyā, matsyākṣī, and śaṅkhapuṣpikā,
kākajaṅghā, śikhiśikhā, brahmadaṇḍī, and ākhuparṇikā,
varṣābhū, kañcukī, mūrvā, mācīka, utpala, and ciñcikā,
śatāvarī, dvilatā, vajrakanda, and karṇikā,
maṇḍūkaparṇī, pāṭhālī, citraka, and grīṣmasundara,
kākamācī, mahārāṣṭrī, haridrā, and tilaparṇikā,
the two white arkas, śigru, dhattūra, mṛgadūrvā, and harītakī,
guḍūcī, musalī, puṅkhā, bhṛṅgarāj, and red citraka,
nāraṅga, sūraṇa, muṇḍī, and the excrement of pigeon and kokila,
rock salt, white varṣābhū, khāpara, hiṅgu, and mākṣika,
viṣṇukrāntā, somavallī, brahmaghnī, and yakṣalocanā,
vyāghrapādī, haṃsapādī, vṛścikālī, and kutumbaka,
svayībhuk, kusuma, kumbhī, hastiśuṇḍī, and indravāruṇī,
and the seeds of arūṣkara too: all these are niyāmikās.

children.text: etāḥ samastā vyastā vā deyā saptadaśādhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, all together or separately, should be applied in groups of more than seventeen.
They should be employed in the killing, stupefying, and binding of <s>rasa</s>.
The niyāmaka herbs, ground with the urine of a cow that has not calved, are mūrvā and the rest.

children.text: taddrāvair mardayet sūtaṃ yathā pūrvoditaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: With their liquids one should rub <s>sūta</s>, in the order stated earlier.
Thus the killing procedure joined with digestion has been described.
Removing the good stalk of a bījapūra fruit, make a small opening.
Put in one salted nirodhaka and cover it with that.
A pot filled with sour gruel should be heaped with the juice of lemons.
In the middle of it, by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>, the bījapūraka should be immersed.

children.text: baddhvā pidhāya saptāhaṃ haṭhāgniṃ jvālayed adhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bound and covered it, one should kindle a forced fire beneath for a week.

children.text: pratyahaṃ mātuliṅgaiś ca navyair bhavyabhavan mukham ||
children.translated_text: Every day, with fresh mātuliṅgas, its mouth becomes excellent and effective.
With its mouth opened by <s>sūta</s>, it swallows mica and the like.

children.text: vyāttavaktro grasatyeva kṣiptaṃ sarvaṃ ca jīryati ||
children.translated_text: Open-mouthed, it swallows whatever is thrown in, and everything is digested.
With karkoṭī, phaṇinetrā, ciñcikā, ambuja, and arka substances,
it should then be properly restrained, and its restlessness should be removed.
But when it has been weakened, it becomes afflicted by rubbing, stupefying, and distilling.

children.text: sṛṣṭyambujair nirodhāt taladvayaprāyo na khaṇḍaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Because it is confined by the sṛṣṭyambujas, it should not be broken, being generally in two lower layers.

children.text: itthaṃkadarthitatanurgalitātmavīryaḥ sṛṣṭyāṃ citaś chagaṇakaiḥ puṭito balī syāt
children.translated_text: When its body has thus been afflicted and its own vigor has ebbed away, if it is heaped in sṛṣṭi and cooked in a closed vessel with cow-dung cakes, it becomes strong.
With pastes of bhūṭaṅkaṇa, uṣaṇa, svayāsurī, and śigru,
when steamed for three days in husk-water, it then becomes very blazing.
Triphalā, citramūla, saurāṣṭrī, and navasādara
should be moistened with śigru juice, and one should rub it for three days.

children.text: tenaiva madhyagaṃ kṛtvā niyamyo'sau punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed it in the middle with that very substance, one should restrain it again and again.
When the thirteenth day has arrived, an excellent stimulant is produced.
With bhū-khaga, ṭaṅkaṇa, manaḥśilā, salt, āsurī, śigru, and sour gruel, for three days,
by steaming, that low-burning <s>sūta</s> becomes eager for a morsel.
Into a glass bottle with an open mouth, one should put salted lemon juice

children.text: palaṃ dhānyābhrakaṃ kṣiptvā limped vastramṛdā mukham ||
children.translated_text: and one pala of dhānyābhraka, and smear the mouth with cloth and clay.
At the mouth one should place a small cup, or a small pot filled with sand.
Having placed the bottle in the middle of sand, one should also put sand above it.
Then, below, for eight yāmas, the wise man should kindle a forced fire.
One pala of dhānyābhraka should be digested day and night.
The knower of <s>rasa</s> should digest dhānyābhra in eight times the quantity of <s>sūta</s>.
That mercury is called by name the gaganagrāsa.
After that, all the mica should be made into single leaves.
Placed on a heated potsherd, it should be burned with an intense fire.
With water of agasti flowers and with the juice of kumuda flowers,
with varṣābhū, taṇḍulīya, marica, and sumukha,
then, having processed the mica with buffalo milk,
and having washed it with yavaciñcikā water, one should cook it in a puṭa.
With powders of marica, āsurī, siddhārtha, and viṣa, the <s>sūtaka</s>
should be steamed, bound in sour gruel, in a swing-apparatus for three days.

children.text: evaṃ svinno rasaḥ paścāt kāñjike yavaciñcikām
children.translated_text: When the <s>rasa</s> has thus been steamed, afterwards the expert should crush
yavaciñcikā, together with root and leaves, in sour gruel, and combine it.
In sour gruel it is produced constantly in the binding of the divine <s>rasa</s>.
Gold-making is done at the mouth of gold, and in silver the mouth of silver is made.
The wise man should steam it repeatedly with yavaciñcikā water.
At the tip of iron he should make it whirl and should sprinkle śāla wood, well burned, likewise.
The mark of what has been digested should be known as that of a leech holding a staff.
At the second stage it is like crow droppings; at the third it becomes oily.
It is tawny, then without belching, and it releases no droplets.
When held in fire, indeed, the smelled residue is the mark of digested vyoma.
Then, from contact with an altered substance, toward the mouth of the divine herb,

children.text: atha ha carati kṣipraṃ kṣaṇādeva nibadhyate ||
children.translated_text: then indeed it moves quickly and is bound in a single instant.
After that, the wise man should steam the <s>rasa</s>, washed with pleasantly warm āranāla,
standing in an iron bowl, with a gentle fire.
Thus, when the <s>rasa</s> has digested mica,

children.text: viḍaṃ dadyāc ca vidhivaj jārayet taṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the expert should add viḍa in the amount of one eighth, according to rule, and digest it.

children.text: evaṃ ṣaḍguṇajīrṇaṃ tu sūtakaṃ jārayet budhaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the wise man should digest <s>sūtaka</s> that has digested six times its quantity.
That which quickly adheres to the ground is called dhānyābhraka.
When twice as much mica has been digested, it goes off under the guise of smoke.
When four times as much has been digested in it, its power of movement is obstructed.

children.text: utplutyotplutya bāhye ca mūṣāyāḥ patati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Leaping up again and again, it surely falls outside the crucible.

children.text: jīrṇe ca ṣaḍguṇe sūtaṃ kampate 'sau muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: And when six times as much has been digested, that <s>sūta</s> trembles again and again.

children.text: bāhye coḍḍīya no yāti sthitaḥ sthāne sthirāyate ||
children.translated_text: It does not fly away outside, but remains in place and becomes steady.
When eight times as much has been digested in it, the blown mercury grows calm.
Blown with a forced fire, it becomes fixed like stabilized gold.
If silver gadyāṇakas and yāca are smeared with this and melted,
the gold becomes of ten colors, as stated by the knowers of <s>rasa</s>.
The leaves of mica, finely powdered,
are to be rubbed for three days with the watery juice of karpāsī.
One should also rub it with the vāra water of mātuliṅga and kanaka,

children.text: kṣiptvā ṭaṅkaṇakṣāraṃ ca navasāraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: having added ṭaṅkaṇa alkali and likewise navasāra.
Then, having put it in the mortar, one should rub it every day

children.text: rasaiḥ pūrvoditair bhūyo yāvat tad gilate sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: again with the juices mentioned before, until it clearly swallows that.
Yava, kadalī, śigru, ciñcā fruit, punarnavā,
and śatamūlā: mica treated with their juices a sage-number of times,

children.text: tadgrāsaṃ rasarājo'sau sukhaṃ bhuṅkte vare mukhe
children.translated_text: that <s>rasarāja</s> easily consumes as a morsel when the excellent mouth has been produced,
indeed for the sake of bodily perfection and for the sake of metallic perfection.
If <s>sūta</s> easily takes even a little mica,
it is bound, staying inside its own house, like an exceedingly restless thief.

children.text: kumārī kadalī vajrī jārī hemapādī naṭī
children.translated_text: Kumārī, kadalī, vajrī, jārī, hemapādī, and naṭī,
bṛhatī, agnidamanī, and lāṅgalī, in equal parts,
leaf-mica or mica powder, wild, treated with malanīguṇa,
becomes a paste in <s>rasa</s> when rubbed with heated iron powder.
In an iron mortar with four feet one should place mica that has been swallowed by <s>sūta</s>.
Magnetic iron powder should be one sixty-fourth part of the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kāñjikenaiva saṃddāṣṭaṃ bavveraṃ yac ca thūthakam
children.translated_text: Bavvera and that thūthaka, bitten with sour gruel,

children.text: tattathā vai viḍaṃ proktaṃ candanaṃ rasavedibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are likewise called the viḍa, a candana, by the knowers of <s>rasa</s>.
Grinding it with thūthāviḍa, one should kindle a gentle fire below.
The wise should always digest metal eight times the quantity of the mercury.
If magnetite is not available, one should add powder of sharp iron,

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭitamaṃ cāṃśaṃ jīrṇe jīrṇe kṣipen muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: a sixty-fourth part, and should repeatedly add it as each portion is digested.
That mercury, with the metal digested, becomes like wheat in color and astringent,
bound and able to withstand coloring; and the coloring too becomes digested.
One should place the mercury with digested metal in a four-legged iron mortar,
together with powder, a sixty-fourth part, of ayaḥprakāśa and rāji.
Having ground it with thūthāviḍa, one should kindle a mild fire beneath.
The ayaḥprakāśikā rāji, eight times the quantity of mercury, is to be digested.
When the ayaḥprakāśa and rāji have been digested, yellowness will arise.
And for the purpose of producing redness, one should digest himarāji.
In a four-legged iron mortar, with mercury whose ayaḥprakāśa has been well digested,
one should place powder, a sixty-fourth part, of hemarāji.
Having ground it with thūthāviḍa, one should kindle a mild fire beneath.
Experts should digest hemarāji eight times the quantity of mercury.

children.text: jīrṇāyāṃ hemarājau ca raktatā jāyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: When the hemarāji has been digested, redness certainly arises.
A pit of clay, smeared with lime and thickly coated with powder or with molasses,
and thoroughly dried after being well smeared, is considered the bhūdhara apparatus.
Having placed mercury together with the rāji called digested gold in the bhūdhara apparatus,
one should add purified sulphur powder amounting to a sixteenth part.
At the mouth one should put a koḍīyaka, and on the downward-facing mouth a cover.
One should smear it with cloth and clay, and then kindle a fierce fire.
One should repeatedly add a sixteenth part, and likewise repeatedly add the koḍīyaka,
until purified sulphur, six times the mercury, is digested.

children.text: bhaved dārḍhyaṃ ca rāgena jīrṇe sūtena gandhake
children.translated_text: When the sulphur has been digested by the mercury, firmness and coloring arise.

children.text: rūpyaṃ tāmraṃ tathā lohaṃ vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ ca pittalam ||
children.translated_text: Silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, and brass,
and bell-metal: these seven metals should be smeared with the mercury and melted.

children.text: tithivarṇaṃ bhavaty evaṃ suvarṇaṃ naiva saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way they become gold of the color of the lunar day; there is no doubt.
Chalk, salt, red ochre, and jīraka

children.text: saṃśodhane suvarṇasya tv imāḥ syuḥ pañca mṛttikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are said to be these five earths for the purification of gold.
Having put mercury with digested sulphur into the bhūdhara apparatus,
one should add the essence of realgar, a thirty-second part relative to the mercury.
At the mouth one should put a koḍīyaka, and on the downward-facing mouth a cover.
One should smear it with cloth and clay, and then kindle a fierce fire.
As each portion is digested, the purifier of mercury should repeatedly add an eighth part.

children.text: sūtatulyaṃ tv idaṃ jāryaṃ na tu hīnaṃ na cādhikam ||
children.translated_text: This is to be digested in a quantity equal to the mercury, neither less nor more.
When the essence of realgar has been digested, I shall state the five earths:
in burning, cutting, astringency, turning, and purification, gold is purified.
One should place the mercury with digested realgar essence in a four-legged iron mortar,
together with powder of khāpara essence, a sixty-fourth part.
Having ground it with thūthāviḍa, one should kindle a mild fire beneath.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe muhuḥ kṣiptvā jāryam aṣṭaguṇaṃ rasāt ||
children.translated_text: As each portion is digested, adding it repeatedly, one should digest eight times the mercury.

children.text: jīrṇe puṣpākṣasattve ca sasneho jāyate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: When the essence of puṣpākṣa has been digested, the mercury becomes oily.
The mouth called annapatha is digested, and henceforth the mercury rises upward.
Of the three annapatha-mouths, from the middle one, a diamond,
with the mercury by which the essence arising from puṣpākṣa has been fully digested,

children.text: prakṣipya lohasattve tau catuṣpāda ubhāv api
children.translated_text: should be placed into the metal essences, both of them in the four-legged vessel.
Grinding with thūthāviḍa, one should kindle a mild fire beneath.
The fire should be kindled only so long as that diamond too is digested.
When the diamond has been digested in the annapatha, the mercury becomes all-pervading.
Mercury of this kind becomes capable of the terrible destruction.
Whatever is given to it, whether rasa, uparasa, or vātaka,

children.text: tatsarvaṃ grasate vegāt yathā devo maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: it swiftly devours all that, just as the god <s>Maheśvara</s> does.

children.text: kṣaṇena jāyate jīrṇaṃ tanmukhe patitaṃ tu yat ||
children.translated_text: Whatever falls into its mouth becomes digested in a moment.
Gems, ending with crystal and magnetite, are digested with extreme speed.
Then, when a crore-fold quantity has been digested, the mercury becomes capable of piercing conch-shell.

children.text: tatkṣaṇād amaratvaṃ ca khecaratvaṃ dadāti ca
children.translated_text: At once it gives immortality and the ability to move through the sky.

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ tumbābījaṃ tu sūtakaṃ yastu vātayet
children.translated_text: But he who applies mercury whose tumbā seed is undigested

children.text: brahmahā sa durācāro mama drohī maheśvari ||
children.translated_text: is a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, ill-conducted, and hostile to me, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
Therefore, with every effort, one should kill mercury only after it has been digested.

children.text: saṃsthāpya gomayaṃ bhūmau paścāt mūṣāṃ tadopari ||
children.translated_text: Having placed cow-dung on the ground, one should then set a crucible upon it.

children.text: tanmadhye kaṭutumbyotthaṃ tailaṃ dattvā rasaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Into its middle, after putting oil produced from bitter tumbī, one should add the mercury.
The juice of kākamācī should be given next, equal in measure to the oil.

children.text: gandhakaṃ vrīhimātraṃ ca kṣiptvā taṃ ca nirodhayet
children.translated_text: After adding sulphur the size of a grain of rice, one should enclose it.
On its back one should place a receiver until it is completely full, O excellent physician.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ ca taṃ jñātvā jīrṇaṃ tailaṃ ca gandhakam
children.translated_text: Knowing it to be cooled of itself, and knowing that the oil and sulphur have been digested,

children.text: kākamācīdravaṃ cāgniṃ dattvā dattvā tu jārayet ||
children.translated_text: one should digest it by repeatedly adding kākamācī liquid and fire.

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ gomayaṃ sārdraṃ dattvā cādho'tha pāvakam
children.translated_text: Having put moist cow-dung on the crucible, one should then apply fire below.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaṃ gandhakaṃ jāryaṃ sūtasyaivaṃ muṣaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Six times as much sulphur should be digested; in this way mercury becomes crucible-processed.
That mercury should be rubbed in a mortar for a day with liquids produced from lemons.
First a sixty-fourth part, and then again a thirty-second part,
and then a sixteenth part of purified gold leaf should be digested into the mercury.

children.text: sāgre sāgre tu tanmardyaṃ jambīrāṇāṃ dravair dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: At each successive increase it should be rubbed firmly with lemon juices.
In the absence of bile and oil, root, salt, and sulphur are used.
One should smear the gold leaf, to be ground, with lemon water.

children.text: ityevaṃ jāraṇā kāryā tataḥ sūtaṃ vimārayet ||
children.translated_text: When digestion has been done in just this way, then one should kill the <s>sūta</s>.
Or else one should digest this without a crucible, by means of the viḍa compound.
I shall declare the viḍa here; the best physician should prepare it.
Powder of conch should be impregnated for a day in the sun with the milk of arka.
In the same way dhūmasāraka should be treated for one day with liquids produced from lemon.
Sauvarcala salt should be decocted for four yāmas with goat's urine.
Kaṇṭakārī juice should be decocted for one day in human urine.
Sājīkṣāra, kāsīsa, tintiṇīka, and śilājatu
are each to be impregnated with liquids from lemon for four yāmas.
The jepāla seed, stripped of its skin, is to be treated for a day with the liquids of radishes.
Rock salt, ṭaṅkaṇa, and guñjā are to be treated for a day with the liquid of śigru root.
All this, in equal parts, should be ground with liquids produced from lemon.
One should carefully preserve that ball; this viḍa is the submarine fire.
With this one should rub <s>sūta</s>; in a heated mortar it consumes it.
It consumes gold, mica, all metals, and their essences in an instant.
The first is called garbha, the next piṇḍa, and the third pariṇāma.
Within <s>sūta</s>, the method of digesting all digestible substances is threefold.

children.text: jārye tu jārite sūte vastreṇa gālite sati
children.translated_text: When the substance to be digested has been digested in <s>sūta</s> and filtered through cloth,

children.text: vastre tiṣṭhati cet sarvamādyo vai garbhasaṃjñakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if all of it remains in the cloth, the first is indeed known as garbha.
But when the again-digested digestible substance passes completely out through the cloth,
with only a little excess in the <s>sūta</s>, it is known as the upper piṇḍa state.
When it makes a net in the <s>sūta</s> and again comes out through the cloth,

children.text: saṃsthite ca nije laulye jīrṇajāryas tṛtīyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when it has settled in its own fluidity, that third is the fully digested digestible substance.

children.text: kumbhasyādhaḥ kṛte chidre dvigranthiṃ dorakaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having made a hole in the bottom of a pot, one should insert a cord with two knots,

children.text: ekaṃ madhye paraṃ bāhye kumbhe kāryo galadghaṭī ||
children.translated_text: one in the middle and the other outside; the pot should be made into a dripping vessel.
Then, with śrīkhaṇḍa from the roots of mahoḍāka in the pot,
having placed in an iron pan <s>pārada</s> that has digested diamond,
and having put on a perforated cover, with the pot filled with śrīkhaṇḍa,
one should place fire on the cover, set sloping downward, and forcefully kindle it.
For four yāmas below the pan, through the middle of the hole in the cover,
the śrīpiṇḍa, falling from the cord, repeatedly drops into the <s>pārada</s>.
Mixed with that burnt <s>sūta</s>, a white ash is produced.
One should put it into a blind crucible together with honey, ghee, and ṭaṅkaṇa.

children.text: dhmātaṃ satkurute bandhaṃ pāradasya na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When blown, it certainly effects the binding of <s>pārada</s>; there is no doubt.
It does not diminish though blown again and again, having reached extreme fixity.
And the <s>sūta</s> that, while being digested, binds itself by itself

children.text: sa hi siddharasānāṃ hi dehaloho nibadhyati ||
children.translated_text: is indeed among perfected <s>rasas</s>; it binds body and metal.
In the black eyes of a deer it causes growth, and in a blind eye it produces sprouting sight.
When the two eyes are anointed with <s>rasa</s>, their pain disappears and the blind person sees.
For the one whose <s>rasa</s> is held in the mouth, among gods, demons, gandharvas, siddhas, guhyakas, and sky-goers,

children.text: raso vaktre sthito yasya tadgatiḥ khe na hanyate ||
children.translated_text: his motion in the sky is not obstructed.

children.text: mriyate na viṣeṇāpi dahyate naiva vahninā
children.translated_text: He does not die even from poison, nor is he burned by fire.
For one perfected in the sky-science, the dead comes back to life in that very instant.
Greater than gems, mantras, and medicines is its surpassing power.
The <s>rasabandha</s> called reviver of the dead is thus proclaimed.
A wise man should melt sixty-four palas of bound <s>sūta</s>.
He should separately melt sixty-four palas of gold filings.
He should pour those gold filings over the liquid of bound <s>sūta</s>.
In this way red ṣoṭa is produced; the process is considered sāraṇa.
Having placed the <s>rasa</s> within silver, one should distill it as before.
It is triturated together with gold paste and rubbed with the juice of kumārī.
It should certainly be smeared on the bottom of the vessel above.

children.text: evaṃ tu gandhakaṃ tāmrarajate hāṭake tathā
children.translated_text: Thus, with sulfur, copper, silver, and likewise gold,
it should be distilled again and again; then one should make it circulate in this way.
As many gadyāṇas of red ṣoṭa as there are when sāraṇa has been performed,
twice that amount of purified śilā, repeatedly and finely powdered, is required.
That powder should be placed above and below in a broad glass flask.
The red ṣoṭa is placed in its womb, with an abhra-cācikā for it.

children.text: kūpikāyāṃ veṣṭanāni sapta deyāni ca mṛdaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven wrappings of clay should be applied to the little flask.
Having dug a pit of a man's measure, filled with cow-dung cakes,

children.text: tadgarbhe kūpikāṃ kṣiptvā haṭhāgniṃ jvālayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: one should place the little flask in its hollow and then kindle a forced fire.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ ca tad grāhyam etanmāraṇam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, it should be taken out; this is called killing.
<s>Sūta</s>, processed and killed with the eighteen saṃskāras,

children.text: khalve kṣiptvā sa sampiṣṭaḥ procyate pratisāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: is placed in a mortar and well ground; this is called pratisāraṇa.
Gold killed with dead lead, and also its powder,
which is to be added in pratisāraṇa: this is called krāmaṇa.
With a leaf of nāgavallī, that other material, though the reading is corrupt, is to be treated.
One should add a rati-measure and make a wrapping of lead leaf.
Then, after melting that powder, one should cast it into all metals.
When they are being melted, it protects them; it is a penetrator of a thousandfold quantity.
When a gadyāṇa of lead has been melted, one should add a gadyāṇa of <s>sūta</s>.
Into the middle of that powder a gadyāṇa of sulfur is also to be added.
When a gadyāṇa of sarjikā is combined, there will be a set of four.
The powder should be thoroughly ground, and then one should stir it with water.
Having placed it in a covered pair of earthen dishes, with cloth and clay leaving no opening,
After digging a pit measuring a hasta and filling it with cow-dung cakes,
one should place the covered pair of earthen bowls in the pit and then kindle the fire.
When it has cooled of itself, one should take it out and make it into a fine powder.
Then, when the pierced <s>sūta</s> has been melted, one should add an amount the size of a mustard seed.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte ca sūtasyodghāṭanaṃ jāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, the opening of the <s>sūta</s> certainly occurs.
One part of living copper and two parts produced from purified gold,
three parts in all: one should make a well-prepared rolled sheet.

children.text: nimbukānāṃ rasaiḥ kṣuttvā yannāgaṃ śilayā mṛtam
children.translated_text: The <s>nāga</s> (lead), killed with <s>śilā</s> and ground with lemon juices,
should be applied as a coating to both sides of the inert sheet.
Six parts of <s>citrakūṭa</s> and one part of salt,
having powdered them in equal proportion, one should then fill a pot with them.

children.text: liptaṃ pattraṃ ca tanmadhye bruḍantaṃ cordhvagaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: The coated sheet should be placed in its middle, sinking down and facing upward.
After an inverted bowl has been put on it, one should seal the neck without gaps with clay.
Then one should place an inverted lid over the bowl,
and beneath the pot one should kindle a forced fire below for four yāmas.

children.text: vidhinā hi ca tenaivaṃ pattraṃ phāḍītrayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: By exactly that procedure the sheet becomes three phāḍīs.
Taking the middle phāḍī, one should discard the two side phāḍīs.
From the powder of the middle phāḍī, hemarāji certainly arises.
By adding one sixty-fourth part, it is to be digested from <s>rasa</s> in an eightfold quantity.
<s>Nāgarāji</s> is ordinary, <s>mākṣikī</s> is remembered as middling,
and <s>ghoṣarāji</s> is excellent; what is from <s>prakāśa</s> is superior to that.
One pala of sharp iron, and also two palas of bronze,
nine palas of copper and three palas of brass,
and palas, equal in number to the lunar days, of <s>nāga</s> killed with <s>śilā</s>,
along with thirty palas of crucible material: the wise man should put these in and melt them.
Then seven and a half palas of golden <s>mākṣīka</s>
should be added little by little, and the wise man should melt it slowly.
When it becomes equal to however many parts of copper there are,
the small amount is <s>prakāśarāji</s>; it is declared to be the first.
Bronze powder equal to the powder of sharp iron
should be put into a crucible, melted, and made into a single lump.

children.text: piṇḍādardhaguṇaṃ nāgaṃ kṣiptvā jāryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Lead amounting to half the lump should be added and digested again and again.
When the lead has been digested to six times the bronze, <s>ghoṣarāji</s> arises.
One should separately melt four palas of purified copper,
four palas of <s>thūthā</s>, and four palas of <s>mākṣika</s>.

children.text: palāṣṭānāṃ kṛtaṃ cūrṇaṃ stoke stokena prakṣipet
children.translated_text: The powder made from eight palas should be added little by little,
until copper remains; this is considered the rāji born from <s>mākṣīka</s>.
One should slowly and separately melt it until it is one part of copper.
Eight parts of <s>nāga</s> killed with <s>śilā</s> and four parts of <s>thūthā</s>,
having been ground and powdered, should be added little by little into the copper.
This becomes <s>nāgarāji</s>.
The wise should always make powder from metals raised up by the rājis.
Each rāji produced from them is to be digested from <s>rasa</s> in an eightfold quantity.
Now, the procedure for extracting sattva from <s>khāpara</s>.
One maṇa of <s>rasaka</s> should be boiled with human urine for three days,
dried in the sun, and cooked in milk for one yāma.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ cūrṇīkṛtaṃ tasmin kṣepyo'ṣṭāṃśaḥ khalasya ca
children.translated_text: When dry and powdered, one should add to it one eighth part of <s>khala</s>,
one fourth part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa-kṣāra</s>, and one eighth part of old jaggery.
When it has been prepared, in clay crucibles that are round and shaped like kacūlā,
one should put the crucible containing the powder inside one of them.
In the other, again, one should set a clay tube, fourteen aṅgulas high at the top,
with an opening in the bottom, and place that one facing downward.
All of that should be made airtight all around with cloth and clay.
For extracting sattva, an apparatus with a gourd-tube should indeed be made.
One should place the apparatus in a furnace and, with dead coals from babbūla, khadira, and the like,
fill it completely again and again and blow strongly over and over.
Having held it with suitable supports, with the mouth turned toward the middle of the gourd-tube,
one should continue until everything drawn from the middle of the crucible has come away as veṣāparīyakam.
Now, the procedure for extracting sattva from <s>manaḥśilā</s>.

children.text: śreṣṭhā kaṇayarī khalve peṣyā manaḥśilā budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: The best <s>manaḥśilā</s>, kaṇayarī, should be ground in a mortar by the wise.
Having put it into a glass flask, one should cover its mouth with mica.
On the top one should place burnt stone powder mixed with salt,
and smear the entire flask with cloth and clay.
After breaking a baked pot and setting the clay-smeared flask at its neck,
a forced fire should be kindled beneath for twelve yāmas for one maṇa.
The belly of the flask becomes empty, and the sattva flows down into the neck.

children.text: kumpaṃ bhaṅktvā śilāsattvaṃ grāhyaṃ yatnena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: After breaking the flask, the wise man should carefully collect the sattva of <s>śilā</s>.

children.text: bhāvenāpi mṛto bheko yatra kutrāpi labhyate
children.translated_text: If, by chance, a dead frog is obtained anywhere,
crystal, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa-kṣāra</s>, and its small khoṭā pieces are to be made fine.
Then, having split open the frog's belly, those fine little pieces should be inserted.

children.text: ghṛtatailādinā digdhaṃ sthālyāṃ bhekaṃ kṣipecca tat ||
children.translated_text: The frog, smeared with ghee, oil, and the like, should then be placed in a pot.

children.text: pradhvarāṃ ḍhaṅkaṇīṃ dattvā sthālī bhūmau nikhanyate
children.translated_text: After putting on an inverted lid, the pot is to be buried in the ground.

children.text: bhuvaḥ sthālīṃ samākṛṣya hy atītaiḥ ṣaṣṭivāsaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When sixty days have passed, one should draw the pot up from the earth.

children.text: sthālyā madhyād viśudhyaivaṃ grāhyaṃ tacca samagrakam
children.translated_text: In this way, after purifying it, that entire substance should be taken from the middle of the pot,
put into a mortar, and ground very finely.
Then, having melted a gadyāṇa of snow-born gold of tithi-color,
within it a valla of powdered bheka is to be added by the skilled.

children.text: na bandho jāyate hemno jātaṃ taddravarūpitam
children.translated_text: No binding of the gold occurs; what is produced has the form of a liquid.
This is the gold-druti, as it is said to have been produced by those who know it.
Just as a golden druti arises when a valla is placed inside gold,

children.text: kāntalohe tathā rūpye vaṅge nāge tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: so too in magnetic iron, in silver, in tin, in lead, and likewise
in copper, in all six metals, the powder penetrates sixteenfold.
When any one of the six metals has been melted,
one should add to a gadyāṇa merely a cloth-measure of bheka-powder.
That metal becomes liquid in form, and by its own name it is called a druti.
The druti of the six metals is made by the experts with its proper operation.

children.text: anayā yāni karmāṇi vakṣyante tāni dhātuṣu ||
children.translated_text: The procedures that are done with this in the metals will now be stated.

children.text: pītāṅgādeva dālīṃ ca pañcāṅgāṃ kuru khaṇḍaśaḥ
children.translated_text: From the yellow-limbed plant one should take the five-limbed dālī and cut it into pieces.

children.text: karpare jvālayitvā ca kartavyaṃ bhasma sūkṣmakam ||
children.translated_text: Having burned it in a potsherd, one should make a very fine ash.

children.text: śeṣānte eva pañcāṅgāṃ niśāhvāyāṃ ca vartayet
children.translated_text: At the end, one should also use the five-limbed plant called niśā.
With that very juice, levigations should be given to this ash.
When one gadyāṇa of gold of tithi-color has been melted,

children.text: prakṣipte bhasmano vallaṃ vallaṃ ca prakṣipet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a valla of the ash should be added, and again a valla should be added.

children.text: evaṃ gadyāṇamadhye ca jāryo gadyāṇakaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: In this way, within a gadyāṇa, a gadyāṇa is always to be digested.
Thus gold-druti is produced; this is the procedure for all metals.
One should burn the five parts of white devadālī in a potsherd.
Twenty-one levigations with cow urine are to be given to the ash.

children.text: tataḥ ṣaṭsvapi loheṣu kāryaḥ prāgudito vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in all six metals, the procedure previously stated should be performed.

children.text: jāyate ṣaṭsu loheṣu drutirevaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way druti arises in the six metals; there is no doubt.

children.text: nāgaṃ manaḥśilā hanti haritālaṃ ca vaṅgakam
children.translated_text: Realgar kills lead, and orpiment kills tin.

children.text: hiṅgulena tathā lohaṃ tāmraṃ ca śuddhagandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise cinnabar kills iron, and purified sulfur kills copper.

children.text: rūpyaṃ ca tilamākṣīkaṃ svarṇaṃ nāgena hanyate
children.translated_text: Silver is killed by sesame-mākṣika, and gold is killed by lead.

children.text: yathā tāmravidhiḥ proktaḥ sa vidhiḥ pañcamāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: As the method for copper has been stated, that is the method in the fivefold killing.

children.text: pattraṃ tāmrasya cūrṇaṃ vā kṛtvā muñcetpṛthak sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: A wise man should make copper leaf or powder and set it aside separately.
Powder of purified sulfur, twice as much as the copper,
should be ground with the juice of kumārī, or with milk if that is unavailable.
Inside two cakes of it he should place the copper leaf.
Having put that inside a covered pair of earthen dishes, he should seal it with clay.

children.text: saṃdhiṃ vastramṛdā liptvā kaṭāhe tatkṣipet puṭam ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the joint with cloth and clay, he should place that firing in a pan.
Having put cow-dung cakes in that pan, he should then kindle the fire.

children.text: jvalite śītalībhūte tāmraṃ grāhyaṃ mṛtaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it has burned and cooled, the copper should be taken by the learned as killed.
Now, the making of diamond fit for food in three ways, and its killing in five ways.
One should remove the stalk of a bījapūra citron and make a hollow.

children.text: tanmadhye hīrakaṃ jātyaṃ kṣiptvā vṛntena chādayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed a genuine diamond in it, one should cover it with the stalk.
The whole bījapūra should be wrapped with cloth and clay.
A pit, a hand-measure in length, depth, and breadth,
should be filled with cow-dung cakes, and the bījapūra set in that pit.
One should cover its mouth with a potsherd, then put fire in the middle.
When it has burned and cooled, with ever fresh bījapūras,
this procedure should be performed again and again nine times.
Having rolled it in niśā into a very fine single pellet,
one should place the excellent substance inside that lump, and the lump in a covered pair of earthen dishes.

children.text: bhartavyā prākkṛtā gartā chāṇakaiḥ sthāpitaiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The previously made pit should again be filled with arranged cow-dung cakes.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhaṃ vastramṛlliptaṃ gartāṃ garbhe pacet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its back, smeared with cloth and clay, should be cooked by the wise man in the womb of the pit.
With fresh pellets, one should cook it nine times repeatedly.
Then, from a royal jujube tree, a branch consisting of tender shoots
should be taken, and the skilled man should make a hole in its interior.

children.text: nesahiṅgum adhaścordhvaṃ dattvā taṃ hīrakaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having put nesa-hiṅgu below and above, he should place that diamond there.
Then, with cloth and clay, the branch with tender shoots should be made without openings.
In the previously mentioned pit it should be processed nine times according to the former method.
Then, after making a hole in a lump made of nesa-hiṅgu,
having placed the diamond and covered its mouth with hiṅgu, a platform of muṣarī-māṣa paste
is put into a vessel filled with that oil, and fire should be kindled below.

children.text: yuktyaivaṃ navadhā kāryaṃ hiṅgukhoṭe nave nave ||
children.translated_text: By this method it should be done nine times, each time in a fresh lump of hiṅgu.

children.text: vidhinā tripatho jātyo hīrako jāyate sphuṭam
children.translated_text: By the procedure of the three paths, a genuine diamond clearly comes into being.
A wise man grinds it with thūthāviḍa and digests it in <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: karṇebhyo mahiṣīnāṃ ca malā grāhyāḥ samagrakāḥ
children.translated_text: The complete dirt from the ears of buffalo-cows should be taken.

children.text: taiśca sampattido hīrān jātyān saṃveṣṭayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: With that, a wise man should wrap genuine diamonds that bestow wealth.
Putting that into small tubers of sūraṇa and wrapping it with cloth and clay,
a firing like a kukkuṭa-puṭa should be given in the ground.
Again and again, with ear-dirt, with small tubers of sūraṇa,
and with fresh cloth and clay, firings are to be given.
By twenty-one times, with kukkuṭa-like firings in the ground,
diamonds are easily made fit for food by the learned.

children.text: yā bhūmyā mardakī tasyā mṛdupattrāṇi vartayet
children.translated_text: One should roll the soft leaves of the plant of the earth called mardakī.
Having placed the diamonds inside that lump, one should make a ball.
Putting it in a covered earthen dish and sealing the joint with cloth and clay,
a firing like a kukkuṭa-puṭa should be given in the ground.
Again and again with fresh, fresh materials, sixty-four firings in all are to be given.
Only kukkuṭa-like firings should be given, and the diamonds should be made fit for food.

children.text: agninā dahyate naiva bhajyate na hato ghanaiḥ
children.translated_text: It is not burned by fire, not split, and not destroyed by blows with hammers;

children.text: jale bruḍati naivāyaṃ duḥśakyo hi parīkṣitum ||
children.translated_text: it does not sink in water; indeed this one is difficult to test.

children.text: līlakaṃ hastayoḥ kṣiptvā hīrakānāṃ ca viṃśatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thrown twenty diamonds into līlaka held in the hands,

children.text: hastābhyāṃ mardanīyāste na syur nistejasaśca ye ||
children.translated_text: they should be rubbed with both hands; those that do not become lustreless are genuine.

children.text: yeṣvekā na bhavedrekhā te jātyā hīrakāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Those on which there is not a single line are remembered as diamonds by birth, genuine diamonds.
Having brought a baked potsherd, many hollows should be made in it.
One should put genuine diamonds in them, and then with mṛtajīvins,

children.text: dhmātvā dhmātvā śikhivarṇaṃ kāryaṃ tajjñaiśca karparam ||
children.translated_text: by blowing again and again, the potsherd should be made peacock-colored by experts.
Human urine and thauhara milk should be mixed together in equal measure.

children.text: tābhyāṃ vidhmāpayed dhmātaṃ karparaṃ ca muhurmuhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: With those two, one should repeatedly quench the blown and heated potsherd.
Then, after making hollows in fresh potsherds, the same diamonds

children.text: tāneva dhmāpayet kṣiptvā dhmātān miśreṇa chaṇṭayet ||
children.translated_text: should be put in and blown, and when heated they should be sprinkled with the mixture.
By this method one should blow and quench them repeatedly seven times.

children.text: tādṛśāḥ prathame dhmāne jāmbulāḥ syur dvitīyake ||
children.translated_text: In the first blowing they become jāmbula; in the second,
lustreless; in the third and fourth, triangular and round;
in the fifth, split into small pieces; the diamonds are certainly cut apart.

children.text: hastābhyāṃ marditāḥ ṣaṣṭhe bhajyante saptame punaḥ
children.translated_text: In the sixth they are broken when rubbed with the hands, and again in the seventh
they have become ash. Thereafter their ash should be placed in a kumpaka vessel.
Gandhaka, the substance called amalāsāra, haritāla, manaḥśilā,
and fourthly suvarṇamākṣika should be made in equal quantities.
Grinding the four with water, one should make them like rāba.
One should set in motion the flowers of puṣpālī and ghana flowers in nisāhā.
Then, having made a lump of the ground paste, one should put genuine diamonds in its middle,
make it into a ball, and place it inside a diamond-crucible.
When that crucible has been blown until it shines fire-colored, one should repeatedly put it into the rāba.
In this way this procedure should be performed fourteen times.

children.text: anāyāsena vajrāṇi bhasmāni syur na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Without difficulty the diamonds become ashes; there is no doubt.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ vidhāya teṣāṃ ca prakṣipetkumpake sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made their powder, the wise man should place it in a kumpaka vessel.
The stamens of ketakī flowers alone, in nisāhā, without water,

children.text: vartayitvā raso grāhyo vastrapūto hi nirmalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be rolled, and the <s>rasa</s> (mercurial liquid), purified through cloth, should be taken clear.
With this <s>rasa</s>, manaḥśilā should be rolled very finely.
Having wrapped the diamonds with it, one should put them inside a diamond-crucible.
After heating and quenching with arka milk, when it has been blown and made fire-like,
this procedure should be carried out repeatedly in this way, as desired, seven times.
Good diamonds are killed and become easy to process, certainly.
That powder, produced from killed diamonds, should be placed in a kumpa vessel.
The white mandāra and arka plants: their roots should be burned.
While they are burning, mṛtajīvins should be made with them.
In those, coated with agāra, little hollows should be carefully made.
Having set the diamonds in them, one should place them in a golden fire-vessel.
With āmbilī, āuli, and babula, together with mṛtajīvins,
after blowing good diamonds with fire, one should put them into a decoction of kulattha beans.

children.text: sukhenātha tayā yuktyā māryaṃ te hīrakā budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, by that method, those diamonds should be killed easily by the learned.

children.text: bhasmībhūtaṃ tu vastrāṇi cūrṇaṃ kṣepyaṃ ca kumpake ||
children.translated_text: The powder that has become ash should be put into cloths and then into a kumpaka vessel.
One should bring the roots of mukhāulī combined with fire.
Śrīkhaṇḍa should be rubbed with them, and with half of it one should make a coating.
A genuine diamond should be put in a diamond-crucible, in the womb of taraṅga.
Having put in the remaining half of the śrīkhaṇḍa, one should place the crucible on the fire-brick.
Having blown it and made it like fire, one should pour it with vajri milk.
Then by this method genuine diamonds are easily killed.
When this has been done, the wise man should place their powder in a kumpaka vessel.
The efficacy that will arise from work with diamond ash will be stated next.
One should put milk in a pot and bind a loose dāthara above it.

children.text: dāthare gandhakaṃ kṣiptvā lipetkaṇṭhaṃ mṛdā dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Having put sulfur in the dāthara, one should firmly smear the neck with clay.
Having placed fire above as well, one should heat it for two ghaṭikās,

children.text: yāvad vyeti payo madhye sa śuddho gandhako bhavet ||
children.translated_text: until it passes down into the milk; that becomes purified sulfur.
Or, in a karṣa-sized kuṇḍalikā, after anointing the sulfur with ghee,
one should place it below and heat until it becomes like oil.
When it has an oily appearance, it is poured into milk and becomes purified sulfur.
Purified by the two methods, it is authorized for work with <s>rasa</s>.
Whatever small copper vessel there is should be washed with the juices of lemons.

children.text: kṛtvā cātyujjvalaṃ tatra śuddhaṃ rasarantīṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made it very bright, one should place purified rasa-rantī in it.
After putting in purified gandhaka-rantī, one should rub it with a finger.
By this method a piṭhā of sulfur and mercury should be made repeatedly.
Of gandhaka-amalāsāra and of purified <s>rasa</s>,
twenty gadyāṇas of each should be rubbed together in a mortar.

children.text: tān kṛtvā kajjalīṃ sūkṣmāṃ vāsasā gālayettataḥ
children.translated_text: Having made them into a fine kajjalī, one should then filter it through cloth.
With the juice of the bulbs of hemavallī, or with śrīkhaṇḍa juice,

children.text: piṣṭvā syāt kajjalīpiṣṭaṃ pīṭhī prakṣālya sārajā
children.translated_text: when it is ground, the paste becomes kajjalī-paste; after washing, the piṭhī is born of sāra.
Having observed the two methods, the piṭhī is produced from sulfur.
The soft rolled leaves of pātāla, with gurutman,

children.text: piḍyāṃ piṣṭasya kṣiptvaināṃ pīṭhīṃ kṛtvā ca golakam ||
children.translated_text: having put this piṭhī into a lump of the ground paste and made it into a ball,
one should place that in a covered earthen-dish firing, sealing the joint with cloth and clay.
A kukkuṭa firing should be given with dense blazing coals.
When it has cooled of itself, the wise man should throw the powder into a small flask.
And sixty-four gadyāṇas of silver should be melted likewise.
When one gadyāṇa of pīṭhī-powder is placed in the midst of that,
it certainly becomes gold of the tithi color; there is no doubt of this.
Thus this is the pīṭhī born from sulfur, capable of piercing one sixty-fourth part.
When combined, the operations that make gold are indeed produced.
One should take excellent sarjikā, and a fourth part of the finely powdered apāna material.

children.text: kṣiptvā sthālyāṃ hi saṃdhyāyāṃ kumbhamānaṃ jalaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having put it in an earthen pot at evening, he should add a kumbha-measure of water.
The kāba-sammanīta arya-sajjikā water is to be discarded.
With excellent stone they are pierced; their powder is very fine.
One maṇa of the fine powder of sulfur and amala-sāra,

children.text: kṣiptvaivātra hyubhe cūrṇe piṣṭvā caikātmatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: having put both powders here, he should grind them and bring them to unity.
He should put five maṇas in a pot in which there are two measured jars.
Having poured sarjikā-water into another vessel, he should set it over the stove.
The sulfur rises up like castor oil.
Taking it again and again from that pot, he should put it, cooled, into a small flask.
He should place ten gadyāṇas of purified mercury in a bhūdhara apparatus.
He should put one gadyāṇa of sulfur oil at the mouth as a koḍīyaka.

children.text: sandhau vastraṃ mṛdā liptvā caturbhiḥ chāṇakaiḥ puṭam
children.translated_text: Having smeared cloth with clay over the joint, a firing with four cow-dung cakes

children.text: dātavyaṃ cānayā rītyā vāraṃ vāram puṭaṃ śatam ||
children.translated_text: should be given; in this way a hundred firings should be given again and again.
At each firing he should add a gadyāṇa of oil and sulfur.
At the mouth he should put a koḍīyaka, again with fresh cloth and clay.

children.text: tailaṃ sūtena saṃjīrṇaṃ daśaghnaṃ gandhakaṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the oil has been digested by the mercury, and gradually ten times as much sulfur,

children.text: hemarājestato vallyā daśa kṣepyāḥ puṭe puṭe ||
children.translated_text: then ten vallīs of hemarāja should be added at each firing.
A firing should be given by the former method, with four cow-dung cakes each time.
And with the hemarāja and mercury, one karṣa is digested after four firings.
Leaves of purified silver should be smeared with this substance in liquid form,
put into a covered pair of earthen dishes, and its joint smeared with cloth and clay.

children.text: liptvā bhūmau pradātavyaṃ chāṇakaiḥ kaukkuṭaṃ puṭam
children.translated_text: Having smeared it, one should place in the ground a kukkuṭa firing with cow-dung cakes.
It becomes gold of the tithi color; it must be done, there is no doubt.

children.text: bhāgā dvādaśa rūpyasya tathā tāmrasya ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: Twelve parts of silver and likewise sixteen parts of copper
should be melted together, twenty-eight parts in a diamond crucible.
The ingot named Moon-and-Sun is produced; one should make its leaves.
Having smeared pieces one finger wide with the substance called digested hemarāja,
one should put them into a covered pair of earthen dishes and smear its joint with cloth and clay.

children.text: liptvā bhūmau pradātavyaṃ chāṇakaiḥ kaukkuṭaṃ puṭam ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared it, one should place in the ground a kukkuṭa firing with cow-dung cakes.
By the second method it should become gold of tithi color.
Then brass leaves, smeared by this same procedure,
become gold of tithi color by just a kukkuṭa firing.
Thus by sulfur oil gold is produced in three ways.
First the skilled man should make a tube shaped like a cow's udder, held in the middle by circular supports,
and a round diamond crucible.
The sulfur oil, ten times as much, and a karṣa of hemarāja,
by which all that has been digested, he should put the rasa into the crucible.
He should add kaṅguṇī oil so that the mercury sinks.
He should blow the crucible on the fire-brick, filled around with coals.
As much mercury as there is by weight, just that much hemarājikā
should be melted in another crucible and placed inside the diamond crucible.
By the bhūdhara procedure, the ingot is a piercer of a thousand.
A thousand gadyāṇas each of silver, copper, and the other base metals
are to be melted separately; within each of them the product of the ingot
should be added separately, one gadyāṇa at a time, and each becomes excellent gold.
Fine powder of maṇas of excellent sarjikā alkali

children.text: saṃdhyāyāṃ tu maṇaṃ sthālyāṃ kumbhamānaṃ jalaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: should be put into a pot at evening, and a kumbha-measure of water added.
In the morning, after discarding the liquid, he should again add a maṇa.
Thus for six days he should make six maṇas of sarjikā-water.

children.text: nītā ye ca jalaṃ śeṣam atyacchaṃ kurute sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man makes the remaining water that has been brought down exceedingly clear.
The sulfur and amala-sāra too should be ground with that water.
He should make it water-like and the wise man should put it into a flask.
Having wrapped the flask with cloth and clay and placed a mango-leaf stopper at its mouth,

children.text: ahorātraṃ jvalatyagniṃ channā yatra ca cūhyake
children.translated_text: where fire burns day and night in a covered furnace,

children.text: nikṣipya kuṃpakaṃ garbhe rakṣā deyā ṣaḍaṅgulām ||
children.translated_text: he should put the flask in its womb and give protection of six fingers' breadth.
Placed there, in secrecy, for twenty-one days,
the attached sarjikā alkali moves all around inside the flask.
The sulfur, having drunk the water, becomes like coconut water.
This water-born sulfur is famed as hṛti-pīṭhī.
Having ground four vallās of purified mercury for two ghaṭīs
with that yellow water, the mercury becomes ash.
He should smear leaves of purified silver with the mercury by means of this.
He should blow it in a diamond crucible with the bellows and perform the operation.
The silver has become black; eight gadyāṇas of it,
combined with gadyāṇas of excellent gold equal to the number of the sun,
when twenty are melted, become gold of tithi color.
And having put purified mercury in a potsherd, he should kindle a gentle fire below.
For a day and night, with a gentle fire, for twenty-one days,
one should repeatedly drop in natural sulfur and only a drop of water.
Purified mercury, for a day and night, for twenty-one days:

children.text: evaṃ niṣpadyate bandhaḥ sūtaḥ ṣoṭaśca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: in this way the binding is accomplished, and the mercury becomes <s>ṣoṭa</s>.
One should gently roll the leaves of <s>pātāla</s> with <s>gurutman</s>.

children.text: piṇḍyāṃ piṣṭasya te ṣoṭaṃ kṣiptvā kāryo hi golakam ||
children.translated_text: Having put that <s>ṣoṭa</s> into a lump of the ground paste, one should make a ball.
Putting it into a covered pair of earthen dishes, and sealing the joint with cloth and clay,
one should wrap it and give a firing in the ground called a <s>kukkuṭa</s>-puṭa.
With smokeless blazing coals, the <s>ṣoṭa</s> becomes yellow in color.
Sixty-four <s>gadyāṇa</s>s of pure silver should be melted.
When one <s>ṣoṭa-gadyāṇa</s> is cast into the midst of that, it becomes excellent gold.
Here the sulfurous melting, the <s>pīṭhī</s>, penetrates sixty-four times.
One should apply as many leaves of <s>godantī</s> and <s>haritāla</s>
as there are, until they are not split in two; then one should put them into a <s>dolāyantra</s>.

children.text: aśmacūrṇasya yā cāchibhṛtā sthālī tayā dṛḍhā
children.translated_text: A firm pot filled with powdered stone, with its cavity,

children.text: dolāyantre tathā kāryā vastraṃ bundhe lagenna hi ||
children.translated_text: should be arranged likewise in the <s>dolāyantra</s>; the cloth should not touch the bundle.
By one who knows the procedure, they should be steamed for two <s>yāma</s>s with a strong fire.
At the end of the steaming and resteaming, one should wash them with water.
So that blue, yellow, and other black impurities come out from them,
after always drying them in the sun, one should place them in the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
In each apparatus, again and again, they should be steamed for two <s>prahara</s>s.
Then, by the method with salt, through a tube, one should steam them twice.
After that, one should steam them successively in the milk of cows and the like.
Having cut <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s> into pieces, one should steam them also in its juice.
They should be rolled in the auxiliary medium, with a subterranean mare-fire flame applied.
Being very fine and sandal-like, one should steam them also in that juice.
Purified by five purifications, <s>godantī</s> becomes free from poison.

children.text: hṛdutkledamaśuddhyā sā ghūrmāraṃ ca karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: When impure, it causes cardiac oppression, moisture, dizziness,

children.text: tāpaṃ ca nāḍisaṃkocam antastāpaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: heat, contraction of the channels, and internal burning.
Therefore <s>haritāla</s>, made pure beforehand, is like nectar.
Taking four parts of purified mercury and twenty of purified <s>tāla</s>,
and repeatedly adding half a <s>palikā</s> of goat fat,
one should grind twenty-four <s>gadyāṇa</s>s in a mortar for one day.
Putting all that into a small flask, and placing a potsherd cup at its mouth,
one should smear the flask with cloth and clay, with clay-covered cloth.

children.text: ā kaṃṭhaṃ saptadhāveṣṭyaṃ cullyantaḥ prakṣipecca tam ||
children.translated_text: It is to be wrapped seven times up to the neck, and placed inside a stove.
A new stove should be made, narrow and rather high,
so that it appears like a <s>dolāyantra</s>, with half the flask inside the stove.
For one <s>yāma</s> a gentle fire should be applied from half-way up the flask.
Then a strong fire should be kindled until four <s>yāma</s>s have passed.
The essence and the mercury will fly upward and adhere to the neck of the flask.

children.text: tatastaṃ kuṃpakaṃ bhaṅktvā kaṃṭhād grāhyaṃ samagrakam ||
children.translated_text: Then, breaking that flask, one should take the whole mass from the neck.
Putting in half a <s>palikā</s> of pot-fat at every moment,

children.text: saptāhaṃ pratyahaṃ piṣṭvā navīne kuṃpake kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: one should grind it every day for seven days and put it into a new flask.

children.text: saptadhā saptabhiḥ kuṃpaiḥ kāryaḥ prāgvihito vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Seven times, with seven flasks, the previously stated procedure should be performed.
Then on the seventh occasion it attains blackness in the neck.
The particles resembling water that remain in the flask-binding,
all those, being essence, should be taken; they are not to be discarded from the operation.
After weighing them, one should take twice as much purified mercury.

children.text: yāmaṃ khalve dvayaṃ piṣṭvā nimbukena rasena ca ||
children.translated_text: Grinding the two together in a mortar for a <s>yāma</s> with lemon juice,

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ ca prakṣepyo mardane naimbuko rasaḥ
children.translated_text: lemon juice should be poured again and again during the trituration.
Then that <s>pīṭhikā</s>, produced from mercury and <s>tālaka</s>, is formed.

children.text: sthālikāyāṃ ca tāṃ pīṭhīṃ kāṃjikaṃ lavaṇānvitam
children.translated_text: In a pot, one should put that <s>pīṭhī</s>, sour gruel mixed with salt,
and pieces of lemon, and steam it for a day.

children.text: naṣṭaṃ naṣṭaṃ muhuḥ kṣepyaṃ kāṃjikaṃ lavaṇānvitam
children.translated_text: Whenever it is lost or evaporated, sour gruel mixed with salt should repeatedly be added.

children.text: svedottīrṇā ca sā pīṭhī saṃśoṣyā cātape dṛḍhā ||
children.translated_text: When that <s>pīṭhī</s> has come out from steaming, it should be firmly dried in the sun.

children.text: pīṭhīṃ tāṃ ṭaṃkaṇakṣāraṃ samatulyaṃ ca peṣayet
children.translated_text: One should grind that <s>pīṭhī</s> with an equal quantity of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa-kṣāra</s>.
Having made two wax cakes, one should put the <s>pīṭhikā</s> into one of them.

children.text: dvitīyāṃ copari dattvā kāryā veḍhinikā budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Placing the second above it, the learned should make a penetrative covering.

children.text: yāvat taulyā hi sā pīṭhī tat taulyaṃ śuddharūpyakam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is the weight of that <s>pīṭhī</s>, pure silver of that same weight
should be melted in a diamond crucible, and the penetrative covering placed on top.

children.text: dahyate ṭaṃkaṇakṣāro mīṇe dhrāte dṛḍhe sati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>ṭaṅkaṇa-kṣāra</s> burns when the wax is firmly melted.
The orpiment-silver <s>ṣoṭa</s> becomes like a white conch.
One should melt sixty-four <s>gadyāṇa</s>s of copper.

children.text: tanmadhye ṣoṭagadyāṇe kṣipte rūpyaṃ bhaved dhruvam
children.translated_text: When one <s>ṣoṭa-gadyāṇa</s> is cast into the midst of that, it surely becomes silver.
This <s>ṣoṭa</s> has become orpiment-silver, penetrating sixty-four times.
The person who takes a <s>rati</s>-measure every day upon rising in the morning:

children.text: ṣaḍbhirmāsaiḥ praṇaśyanti aṣṭa kuṣṭhā daśāpi hi ||
children.translated_text: within six months, eight kinds of skin disease, even ten, perish.

children.text: udgacchanti navā dantāḥ keśāḥ kṛṣṇā bhavanti ca
children.translated_text: New teeth arise, and the hair becomes black.

children.text: palitaṃ mūlato yāti valināśo bhaved dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Grayness goes away from the root, and the destruction of wrinkles is certain.
<s>Kodrava</s> and <s>vyāghramadana</s>: one should nourish their <s>setikā</s>.
From the middle of the paste, one should take two <s>māṇaka</s>s of the very fine part.
Putting sour gruel in a pot, one should pour in water up to the neck.
After seven days have passed, that becomes extremely sour.
By this method a second water, extremely sour, should be prepared.

children.text: maṇaṃ śvetābhrakaṃ cūrṇaṃ saṃyuktaṃ tena vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: A maṇa of white mica powder, combined with that water,
should be thrown into a mortar and pounded; it becomes yāma-dhānyābhraka.
That dhānyābhraka should be put in water twenty-one times.
After letting it float or settle there, it should then be dried again in the sun.
There should be rālā, borax-alkali, salt, and granular guggulu.
Each is to be in a portion of a maṇa-dīpa; the four together make one maṇa.
There are twenty palas and gadyāṇas of sesame and of jaggery,
a pallikā-pīṭhī of vallas, and two karṣas each of honey and milk.
