Combined with the dhānyābhraka itself, it should be ground again and again.

children.text: daśa gadyāṇakā mātrāḥ pūpāḥ kāryā anekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Cakes should be made in many portions, each measure being ten gadyāṇakas.
Having put one into a rākṣasa apparatus, he should fill it with coals.
When one has been melted, the wise man should put in a second.
All should be melted in sequence over yāmas, and, when cooled by themselves, taken out.
From among them one should draw out the druti, the essence produced from mica.
By this method, even easily, druti is obtained from dhānyābhraka.
White dhānyābhraka powder, measuring two gadyāṇas,
should be placed in a pālī of milk, and the sehula should be made to drink repeatedly.
It should be put into the fermenting liquor of a koṣṭikā, as it goes elsewhere.

children.text: pītvā pītvā hi taddugdhaṃ purīṣaṃ tatra muñcati ||
children.translated_text: After drinking that milk again and again, it releases feces there.
All that feces should be collected after many days have passed.
After weighing it, one should add one quarter part of borax-alkali.
After grinding it with ghee and honey, making it like a paste,
with that the middle of a bottle-gourd tube apparatus should indeed be firmly smeared.
Having filled it with coals, with a crooked-mouthed blowpipe,
one should blow for one yāma; that flask is to face downward.
When the plaster bursts, the druti has arisen, produced from white dhānyābhraka.
A second transformation, an abhraka-druti, should be made by those who know.
Somewhere a dead hare is seen by wandering people, by chance.
From the middle of its head the black substance should be taken.
One should grind forty gadyāṇas of dhānyābhraka.
From that, powder equal in measure to the black substance should be put into the black substance.

children.text: dvayaṃ saṃmardya saṃmardya piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having triturated the two together again and again, he should then make a firm lump.
He should smear a cooking pot with ghee, oil, and the like, and put that lump into it.
A covering lid should be placed on it, without openings, with cloth and clay.
It should be put into a chamber of particles and kept hidden for twenty-one days.

children.text: tanmadhye kṛmayo jātā nityaṃ bhakṣyanti cābhrakam
children.translated_text: Worms are produced inside it, and constantly eat the mica.

children.text: tāpe ca mecakābhāve mriyante ca bubhukṣayā ||
children.translated_text: In the heat, when the black substance is gone, they die of hunger.

children.text: vipannāsu ca sarvāsu śeṣaṃ dhānyābhrakī drutiḥ
children.translated_text: When all have perished, the remainder is dhānyābhraka-druti.
This third transformation is known by experts as dhānyābhraka-druti.
Three methods are well known; a fourth does not occur.

children.text: tisṛṇāṃ yāni karmāṇi vakṣyante tāni sāṃpratam ||
children.translated_text: The operations belonging to the three will now be stated.
Ten gadyāṇas of purified mercury, inside a diamond crucible,
should be placed in a sand apparatus, and a gentle fire should be kindled for a day.
For a day and night, drop by drop, the essence of bhūnāga should be repeatedly added.

children.text: vaktraṃ sūtasya jāyeta dattaṃ sarvaṃ ca jīryati ||
children.translated_text: A mouth is produced in the mercury, and everything that is given is digested.
At night, cilhā should be ground extremely fine.
Having squeezed it out, the rasa should be collected, purified through cloth and very free from impurity.
In a magnetic vessel of such size that it holds one pala of water,
ten gadyāṇakas of mercury whose mouth has been produced should be placed.
Of one among the three drutis, ten gadyāṇas should also be added.
Then the magnetic vessel should be filled to the neck with cilhā-water.

children.text: tacca kāntāyasaṃ pātraṃ yantre vālukake kṣipet
children.translated_text: And that vessel of magnetic iron should be placed in a sand apparatus.
For a day and night a gentle fire should repeatedly be kindled beneath it.
Through the union of the two, this wondrous vajra-ṣoṭa is produced.
Having put it in a diamond crucible, the wise man should blow it with coals.
After placing twenty gadyāṇas of purified silver in the middle,
he should melt it thoroughly, and afterwards draw out the melted material.
It is called Akṣaya, radiant, motionless, and exceedingly pure.

children.text: gururjāto'tha bhagnaśca bhajyate sa hi khoṭakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It becomes heavy and then, when broken, that khoṭaka indeed breaks apart.
One should melt one hundred gadyāṇakas of tin in a diamond crucible.

children.text: tanmadhye ṣoṭagadyāṇe kṣipte rūpyaṃ bhaved dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: When a gadyāṇa of ṣoṭa is placed among it, it certainly becomes silver.
The operation of the threefold mica-druti in tin has a hundredfold power of penetration.

children.text: ṣoṭamadhyād ratimātraṃ yaḥ karoti sadā naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who constantly prepares even a rati measure from the middle of the ṣoṭa,
within six months becomes radiant, pure, and imperishable.
This khoṭa is famous on earth, certainly producing metal and body effects.
The wise man should melt four gadyāṇas of excellent gold.
He should make leaves from them like the petals of jarakīśa.
One pala produced from a human skull and one from datura root,

children.text: candanaṃ ca pṛthak ghṛṣṭvā tulyamekatra miśritam ||
children.translated_text: and sandalwood too, separately rubbed, should be mixed together in equal amount.
One gadyāṇa of diamond ash should be put into the śrīkhaṇḍa mixture.

children.text: khalve saṃpeṣayet tāvad yāvad ekātmatāṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: It should be ground in a mortar until it attains complete unity.
With that very mixture he should smear the gold leaves very firmly.
A gadyāṇa of bhūnāga essence should be put into a blind crucible.
Having placed the gold leaves there as well, the crucible, as appropriate, ...
into the fire-pit chambers, repeatedly filling them without interruption.
He should blow it in a curved-mouthed blowing tube with dead and living coals.
A ṣoṭa consisting of gold and diamond, produced from bhūnāga essence, will arise.

children.text: artayitvā ca taṃ ṣoṭaṃ cūrṇaṃ kāryaṃ susūkṣmakam
children.translated_text: Having heated that ṣoṭa, it should be made into an extremely fine powder.
Then a glass flask, up to the neck, should be wrapped seven times with cloth and clay.
And in its middle he should first put a karṣa measure,
namely the essence produced from bhūnāga; into its middle he should put purified mercury.
Then he should add six gadyāṇas and place it in a sand apparatus.
Having set that apparatus on the stove, he should forcefully kindle the fire below.

children.text: naṣṭaṃ naṣṭaṃ muhuḥ kṣepyaṃ satvaṃ bhūnāgasambhavam
children.translated_text: Again and again, as it is consumed, the essence arising from bhūnāga should be added.

children.text: satvena dravarūpeṇa bhṛtā dhāryā ca kumpikā ||
children.translated_text: The little flask should be kept filled with the essence in liquid form.
The rasa should be steamed for a day and night by the wise man for seven days.
Thus steamed, these six alone, produced from purified mercury, have been heated.

children.text: vaktraṃ sūtasya saṃjātaṃ sūto jātaśca rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: A mouth has arisen in the mercury, and the mercury has become a rākṣasa.
Six gadyāṇas, made from the essences beginning with the former gold creeper,
a sixty-fourth part of them, from their midst, again and again,

children.text: kṣiptvā khalve'pi sūtāntaḥ piṣṭvā piṣṭvā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be put into the mercury in a mortar too, and ground and ground slowly.

children.text: jāraṇīyāḥ ṣaḍevaite śeṣāḥ ṣaṭ sūtajāḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: These six alone are to be digested; the remaining six, produced from mercury, remain.
Six gadyāṇas of excellent mercury, mixed with these,
are to be filtered in twelve crucibles; a ṣoṭa with hundredfold penetrating power will result.
Of silver, copper, and the other base metals, one hundred gadyāṇas each,

children.text: trayāṇāṃ ca śataikasmin pratyekaṃ gālite pṛthak
children.translated_text: and when the hundred of the three has been melted separately in each case,

children.text: tanmadhye ṣoṭagadyāṇaṃ pratyekaṃ ca pṛthak kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: one gadyāṇa of ṣoṭa should be put separately into each of them.
In the three metals gold will certainly arise, of the color of the lunar day.
If, in the morning, he regularly takes a rati measure from the middle of the ṣoṭa, combined with amṛtakalā,

children.text: ādatte niyataṃ velaṃ valistasya na jāyate
children.translated_text: at the fixed time, no wrinkle is produced in him.

children.text: palitaṃ mūlato yāti kṛṣṇāḥ keśā bhavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Gray hair disappears from the root, and the hairs become black.

children.text: śarīre jāyate dārḍhyaṃ śarīraṃ kṣīyate na hi
children.translated_text: Firmness arises in the body; the body does not waste away.
From constant use of the ṣoṭa the body's luster is like gold.
Produced from the three essences of gold, diamond, and bhūnāga and the like,
this wondrous ṣoṭa has come into being, effecting the body and penetrating a hundredfold.
Homage always to glorious <s>Bhairava</s>, lord of the hosts, and to glorious <s>Vāṇī</s>,
by whose grace pills, collyria, and mercuries are accomplished.

children.text: saṃkhyāśītiḥ saturyā syātpratyekaṃ ca pṛthak triṣu
children.translated_text: The number is eighty together with four, separately in each of the three.
Thus the total number of the three will be two hundred and fifty-two.
From within this whole number, in the case of any single one,
from the beginning of the undertaking up to the end result, he should perform uninterrupted tapas.
From one month beforehand, facing downward, up to the completion and even to the fruit,

children.text: brahmacaryaṃ bhuvi svāpaṃ haviṣyānnaṃ ca bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: there should be celibacy, sleeping on the ground, and eating sacrificially pure food.
In rites of tapas, rasas and the like, which are to be accomplished by tapas, are perfected.

children.text: doṣaṃ daivasya yacchanti tapohīnā hi sādhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For practitioners devoid of tapas lay the fault upon fate.
Therefore the pills described in the account were taught by the yogin <s>Śrīkaṅkālaya</s>.
I shall explain the pill whose fruit is knowledge, consisting of fifty-two good vallikās.
Four of mica essence, four of gold pyrites,
four of purified silver, and one valla of hemarājikā,
together with the earlier mercury purified by the eighteen saṃskāras,
make, with it, thirty-nine and fifty-two combined.
Having put all these into a mortar, he should triturate them for seven days.
Again and again, with the fine bhūta-śrīkhaṇḍa of the varuṇa tree,
he should heat it over a gentle fire in a swing apparatus for two days.
Having made that into a pill, he should heat it successively with pañcāmṛta.

children.text: madhvājyaṃ dadhi dugdhaṃ ca śarkarā ceti pañcamī
children.translated_text: Honey, ghee, curd, milk, and sugar: this is the fifth item.

children.text: asmin pañcāmṛte svedyā yāmāṣṭāṣṭā mṛtaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: In this pañcāmṛta it should be heated for eight yāmas each, for each processed substance.

children.text: kāntalohamaye pātre madhunā ca guṭīṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should put the pill with honey into a vessel made of magnetic iron.
That vessel should be set inside a cooking pot filled with sand.
He should place the pot on the stove and kindle the fire below for eight yāmas.

children.text: svedane'yaṃ vidhiḥ kāryaḥ stokake cāmṛte kramāt ||
children.translated_text: This procedure of steaming is to be performed, successively, with a little amṛta.

children.text: naṣṭe naṣṭe muhuḥ kṣepyaṃ kramāt pañcāmṛtaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: Whenever it is consumed, pañcāmṛta should always be added repeatedly in order.
In just the sequence joined with honey, he should steam the pill in five ways.
Devoted to tapas and active in the rite, he should turn it about with his hands.
When completed, the pill should be made as one of fifty-two good vallikās.

children.text: yasyāḥ śuddhāvubhau pakṣau prasūtā cottame kule
children.translated_text: For a woman whose two sides are pure and who is born in a good family,

children.text: brāhmaṇī kṣatriyā vāpi vaiśyī caivaṃvidhā ca yā ||
children.translated_text: whether she is a Brahmin woman, a Kṣatriya woman, or a Vaiśya woman of this sort,
excluding a Śūdra woman, when the first pregnancy of a woman of the three varṇas occurs,
one month afterward that pill should be given to her.
Except at the times for food, medicine, betel, and drink, by her
it should be held in the mouth day and night, continuously for one month.

children.text: māse vīte ca sā pṛṣṭā jñānaṃ vakti trikālajam
children.translated_text: When the month has passed and she is questioned, she speaks knowledge of the three times:
future, past, and present, immediately producing conviction.
This is the efficacy of the pill, producing extreme wonder.
Among people there is a very great excess of power in the rasa-pill.

children.text: yādṛśaṃ svadhiyā jñātaṃ tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: As I have understood it with my own intellect, so have I written it.

children.text: yadi kvacid vyalīkaṃ syāttadā śodhyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If anything should be false anywhere, then it is to be corrected by the discerning.
Thus there was a celebrated rāula named <s>Jāladeva</s>, an ornament of the <s>Yādava</s> lineage.
Born from him was <s>Mahipa</s> by name; his son was called <s>Bhadiga</s>.
His son, named <s>Campa</s>, had splendid beauty and fame, sung by those who know <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: paropakāraikarasaḥ kalāvān manāgajākau kila yasya bandhū ||
children.translated_text: Devoted solely to helping others and skilled in the arts, <s>Managa</s> and <s>Jaka</s>, it is said, were his kinsmen.
